main_text.p: édistū patris mel gustasset,i.Sam.14. I-tem Ionas Propheta, cap.i.

De circūstantijs sortitionis,quibus ueteres sæpiùs usi sunt, ex hisce dictis nonnulla coniicere licet: Proijcere sortes. In sinum proijcere. Certo die sortiri. Sed quia ocio & tempore destituor,isthęc uobis peruestigandā relinquo.
main_text.head: VERSVS VIII.
main_text.p: Dixerunt ergo ad eum: Indica nunc quaso nobis (tu) propter quē hoc malum (acci-Lectio 19.21. Nouembris, 1586. dit) nobis:quod est opus tuum,& unde uenis,& quæ terra tua, & de quónam populo es?

1. Genus & schema orationis plenū humanitatis, & alienum à Cyclopica asperitate. Benignè enim Ionam, forte iam deprehensum, & hauddubiè ualde consternatum, alloquuntur, dolentes, ut res ipsa doceat[?], cum dolente. Simile exemplū habetur Iof.7.19. Dixit Iofua ad Achan: Fili mi, da quæso gloriā Iehouæ Deo Israelis, & da ei confessionē, atq; indica nūc mihi quid feceris, ne abscondas à me.

page.notes: Right margin: "Lectio 19." and "21. Nouembris, 1586." beside the paragraph "Dixerunt ergo ad eum". Page number "8i" uncertain (could be "81"). "doceat" uncertain (print looks like "docer" or "doceat"). Greek word in the "ὑποθέσει" line is read from a small print and may be imperfect. Printed "quē", "gloriā" and "peruestigandā" follow the scan; their macrons are uncertain. Show-through from the reverse side is ignored. The page ends mid-sentence with "Christiā" and continues on the next page.
